evidence.title: Electoral district of Broken Hill
evidence.text: Broken Hill was an electoral district of the Legislative Assembly in the Australian state of New South Wales.

evidence.title: Electoral district of Broken Hill
evidence.text: From 1894 to 1913, the Broken Hill district was covered by the electoral districts of "Broken Hill", Willyama and Sturt.

evidence.title: Electoral district of Broken Hill
evidence.text: In the 1912 redistribution, the electoral district of "Broken Hill" was abolished and absorbed into "Willyama" and "Sturt".

evidence.title: Electoral district of Broken Hill
evidence.text: In 1920, "Willyama", "Sturt" and the electoral district of Cobar were combined to create a three-member "Sturt".

evidence.title: Electoral district of Broken Hill
evidence.text: In 1927, single-member electorates were recreated and the city of Broken Hill was split between "Sturt" and Murray.

evidence.title: Electoral district of Broken Hill
evidence.text: From 1932, the city of Broken Hill was split between "Sturt" and Cobar.

evidence.title: Electoral district of Broken Hill
evidence.text: In 1968 "Sturt" was renamed Broken Hill and included all of the city of Broken Hill.

evidence.title: Electoral district of Broken Hill
evidence.text: In 1999, it was merged with part of "Murray" and renamed the electoral district of Murray-Darling.

evidence.title: Joshua Arthur
evidence.text: Joshua George Arthur (27 January 1906 – 20 May 1974) was an Australian politician who represented the Electoral district of Hamilton (1935–50) and the Electoral district of Kahibah (1950–53) for the Australian Labor Party.

evidence.title: Pru Goward
evidence.text: Prudence Jane Goward (born 2 September 1952 in Adelaide), an Australian politician, is the New South Wales Minister for Family and Community Services and Minister for Social Housing, since January 2017 in the Berejiklian government, and the Minister for Prevention of Domestic Violence and Sexual Assault, since 2015.

evidence.title: Pru Goward
evidence.text: She has previously served as the Minister for Mental Health, Minister for Medical Research, and Assistant Minister for Health between April 2015 and January 2017, and the Minister for Women between 2011 and January 2017, in the second Baird government and the Minister for Planning during 2014 and 2015.

evidence.title: Pru Goward
evidence.text: With the first Berejiklian government she returned to Community Services portfolio which she previously held between 2011 and 2014, in the O'Farrell and first Baird governments.

evidence.title: Pru Goward
evidence.text: Goward is a member of the New South Wales Legislative Assembly representing Goulburn for the Liberal Party of Australia since 2007.

evidence.title: Electoral district of Southern Boroughs
evidence.text: Southern Boroughs was a former electoral district for the Legislative Assembly in the Australian state of New South Wales created in 1856.

evidence.title: Electoral district of Southern Boroughs
evidence.text: It included the towns of Goulburn, Braidwood, Yass and Queanbeyan, while the surrounding rural area were in the electoral districts of Argyle, United Counties of Murray and St Vincent and King and Georgiana.

evidence.title: Electoral district of Southern Boroughs
evidence.text: It was replaced by Goulburn, Braidwood, Queanbeyan and Yass in 1859.

evidence.title: Electoral district of Queanbeyan
evidence.text: Queanbeyan was an electoral district of the Legislative Assembly in the Australian state of New South Wales from 1859 to 1913, in the Queanbeyan area.

evidence.title: Electoral district of Queanbeyan
evidence.text: It replaced parts of the electoral district of United Counties of Murray and St Vincent and the electoral district of Southern Boroughs.

evidence.title: Electoral district of Queanbeyan
evidence.text: It was merged with the electoral district of Monaro in 1913, when much of its former territory had been absorbed in the Australian Capital Territory.

evidence.title: Electoral district of Argyle
evidence.text: Argyle was an electoral district for the Legislative Assembly in the Australian State of New South Wales from 1856 to 1904, including Argyle County surrounding Goulburn.

evidence.title: Electoral district of Argyle
evidence.text: The town of Goulburn was in Southern Boroughs from 1856 to 1859 and then Goulburn.

evidence.text: Buttala electoral district was an electoral district of Sri Lanka between August 1947 and March 1960.

evidence.title: Buttala Electoral District
evidence.text: The district was named after the town of Buttala in Moneragala District, Uva Province.

evidence.title: Buttala Electoral District
